# Products and bands

Every product is a GeoTIFF, described in Python by a small metadata record. The
record holds the product's identity, such as burst, date and type, and
`FileManager.get_product_path()` turns it into the file's location. This page
describes what the files contain.

## Burst products

Each burst product is one GeoTIFF, with its bands named in the band
descriptions:

| Product | Bands | Values |
|---|---|---|
| RTC backscatter | `gamma0`, `scattering_area` | Linear power; area without units |
| GTC backscatter | `beta0` | Linear power |
| Coherence | `coherence` | Magnitude, 0 to 1, without units |
| Interferogram | `ifg_real`, `ifg_imag`, `intensity_primary`, `intensity_secondary` | Uncalibrated |

Backscatter is stored as linear power, not decibels, in products and
composites alike. Convert with
`10 * log10(value)` only after averaging, since the mean of decibels is not the
decibel of the mean. The `scattering_area` band describes how much ground each
pixel covers; [Local resolution weighting](resolution-weighting.qmd) explains
how composites use it.

The interferogram's phase is the angle of the complex number
`ifg_real + i·ifg_imag`, in radians from −π to π. Its two intensity bands show
the brightness of each acquisition.

## Composites

A composite holds one band, the quantity of its inputs: gamma-0, beta-0 or
coherence, in the same units. Its band description is the polarization, such
as `VV`.

With `write_qa=True`, each quality layer of a composite is written to a file of
its own:

- The number of observations (`QA-NUM`) counts the acquisitions that
  contributed to each pixel.
- The composite quality map (`QA-CQM`) rates how fine the combined detail of
  each pixel is, without units. Only LRW composites have it.

[Local resolution weighting](resolution-weighting.qmd#the-quality-layers)
explains both.

## Missing values

Pixels without data are `NaN`, for example outside the burst. Keep them
missing in statistics and plots rather than replacing them with zero. The one
exception is the number of observations, an integer layer that marks pixels
without data as 0. Rasterio returns them masked with
`src.read(1, masked=True)`.

## Metadata tags

Each GeoTIFF also carries tags that say how to read it and how it was made.
They include the units of the stored values, the acquisition dates, the DEM,
and the SNAP and s1bursts versions:

```{.python}
import rasterio

with rasterio.open(fm.get_product_path(product)) as src:
    print(src.descriptions)
    print(src.tags())
```

These tags make a file understandable on its own, even when separated from the
code that wrote it. Their names follow the vocabulary of the
[CEOS-ARD SAR specification](https://ceos.org/ard/), so a term can be looked up
there. s1bursts borrows the vocabulary only and does not claim conformance with
the specification.

## Filenames

A filename holds only what tells one product from another, in fixed fields
joined by underscores. Each product type has its own pattern:

| Product | Filename pattern |
|---|---|
| SLC burst | `S1_SLC_<orbit><pass>_<burst>_<swath>_<pol>_<date>.zip` |
| RTC backscatter | `S1_RTC_<orbit><pass>_<burst>_<swath>_<pol>_<date>_<zone>.tif` |
| GTC backscatter | `S1_GTC_<orbit><pass>_<burst>_<swath>_<pol>_<date>_<zone>.tif` |
| Coherence | `S1_COH<baseline>_<orbit><pass>_<burst>_<swath>_<pol>_<date1>_<date2>_<zone>.tif` |
| Interferogram | `S1_IFG<baseline>_CMPLX_<orbit><pass>_<burst>_<swath>_<pol>_<date1>_<date2>_<zone>.tif` |
| RTC LRW composite | `S1_RTC_LRW[_<qa>]_<square>_<pol>_<start>_<end>.tif` |
| Coherence LRW composite | `S1_COH<baseline>_LRW[_<qa>]_<square>_<pol>_<start>_<end>.tif` |
| RTC or GTC pass composite | `S1_RTC_COMP_<pass>[_QA-NUM]_<square>_<pol>_<start>_<end>.tif`, with `GTC` for GTC |
| Coherence pass composite | `S1_COH<baseline>_COMP_<pass>[_QA-NUM]_<square>_<pol>_<start>_<end>.tif` |

Square brackets mark the part that names a quality layer; the composite itself
has none. The fields are:

| Field | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `<orbit>` | Relative orbit number, three digits | `015` |
| `<pass>` | Pass direction: `A` ascending, `D` descending | `A` |
| `<burst>` | ESA burst ID, six digits | `030346` |
| `<swath>` | Sub-swath | `IW1` |
| `<pol>` | Polarization | `VV` |
| `<date>` | Acquisition date, `YYYYMMDD` | `20220801` |
| `<date1>`, `<date2>` | Dates of the primary and secondary acquisitions of a pair | `20220801`, `20220813` |
| `<baseline>` | Days between the acquisitions of a pair, two digits | `12` |
| `<zone>` | UTM zone of the product's CRS | `32N` |
| `<square>` | MGRS grid square | `32TLS40` |
| `<start>`, `<end>` | First and last day of the composite's period | `20250801`, `20250831` |
| `<qa>` | Quality layer: `QA-NUM` or `QA-CQM` | `QA-CQM` |

The RTC product of the [Quickstart](quickstart.qmd), burst 30346 in sub-swath
IW1 on ascending orbit 15, is named
`S1_RTC_015A_030346_IW1_VV_20220801_32N.tif`, and the number of observations of
an LRW composite is named
`S1_RTC_LRW_QA-NUM_32TLS40_VV_20250801_20250831.tif`.

`FileManager` keeps SLC bursts in `s1-slc`, burst products in `s1-prod` and
composites in `s1-comp`, below the directory it is given.

Processing settings are not part of the name. They are recorded in the tags
instead, and a rerun compares them before it skips an existing file; see
[Reprocessing and failures](processing.qmd#reprocessing-and-failures).
